\*Counts are the sum of the frequencies of the listed title‑word tokens (the top‑20 title words obtained via an aggregation). They give a rough indication of how many issues mention each token, not an exact issue count (issues can contain multiple tokens and many titles contain none of the top tokens).

**How the clusters were obtained**

1. Retrieved the most frequent words from all issue titles (excluding common stop‑words).  
   `aggregate_collection(repo_name="apache_kafka", collection="issues", pipeline=[{ "$project": { "titleWords": { "$split": [ { "$toLower": "$title" }, " " ] } } }, { "$unwind": "$titleWords" }, { "$group": { "_id": "$titleWords", "count": { "$sum": 1 } } }, { "$match": { "_id": { "$nin": ["", "the","a","an","and","or","to","of","in","for","on","with","using","add","update","fix","issue","error","bug","fail"] } } }, { "$sort": { "count": -1 } }, { "$limit": 20 }])` → top‑20 words and their counts.  

2. Grouped those words into a small set of intuitive themes (e.g., “testing”, “streams”, “configuration/usage”, etc.) and summed the counts of the words that belong to each theme.

**Result**

The issue tracker is dominated by a large number of “minor” or “hot‑fix”‑type tickets, followed by many issues that discuss configuration / usage nuances. Testing‑related tickets form a noticeable but smaller group, while Streams‑API, consumer‑related, and core Kafka concepts each have a dedicated set of issues. These clusters give a high‑level view of the main topics that the Apache Kafka community is dealing with.
